source: Diocesan Cycle of Prayer November 1, 2025 – November 30, 2026
sourceFile: "Cycle of Prayer" page, fetched directly from https://edow.org/congregational-resources/worship/cycle-of-prayer/ (rendered HTML, read from its own per-month tab markup rather than a linearized/summarized extraction).
notes: `diocese` field: the page's <title> tag, its og:site_name, and its embedded JSON-LD WebSite/Organization/breadcrumb names all consistently read "Episcopal Diocese of Washington" (no "DC" in the self-identification itself, even though this app's own reserved `dioceseShort` is "washington-dc" to disambiguate from other dioceses named Washington). Used as printed.

Transcribed directly from the live page's rendered HTML (fetched and parsed from its own per-month tab markup), not from a summarized/linearized extraction -- the page presents its cycle as 13 clickable month tabs (June 2026, July 2026, August 2026, September 2026, October 2026, November 2026, December 2025, November 2025, January 2026, February 2026, March 2026, April 2026, May 2026) in that exact scrambled, non-chronological DOM order, evidently a CMS artifact from tabs being appended/reordered over successive years rather than a deliberate editorial order. This file's own `entries` array is instead sorted into true ascending chronological order (Nov 2025 through Nov 2026), per this schema's own expectation that entries are ordered ascending; the raw tab order itself carries no content difference, only presentation order.

Per this schema's own precedent for a source whose range crosses a year boundary (episcopal-tennessee-2026.json, episcopal-california-2026.json, episcopal-nevada-2026.json, episcopal-san-diego-2026.json): the page's own header reads "Diocesan Cycle of Prayer November 1, 2025 – November 30, 2026", and the 9 entries falling in November-December 2025 are a small lead-in (9 of 56 total entries) to the 2026 cycle, not a genuine ~half/half split -- so they are included here in this single '-2026' file (disclose-and-include) rather than split into a companion '-2025' file, matching the Tennessee/California/Nevada/San Diego shape rather than the Southeast Florida two-file shape.

The page's own header claims coverage through "November 30, 2026", but the November 2026 tab's own content stops at the Nov 22, 2026 entry (followed by a trailing blank paragraph in the source's own markup) -- there is no Nov 29, 2026 entry anywhere in the source. Transcribed as printed/absent rather than fabricating a 57th entry to fill out the header's claimed range; the gap between the last real entry (Nov 22, 2026) and the header's stated end date (Nov 30, 2026) is disclosed here rather than silently closed, the same way this corpus's episcopal-tennessee-2026.json disclosed its own stale/mismatched section heading rather than correcting it.

Three printed dates in the source are not actually Sundays, even though every date on either side of them is, and even though each carries a liturgically sequential 'Nth Sunday after Pentecost'/'... of Easter' label consistent with its neighbors: 'Oct 20' and 'Oct 27' (both print as the correct next ordinals -- 21st and 22nd Sunday after Pentecost -- but the actual Sundays for those ordinals are Oct 18 and Oct 25, 2026) and 'Apr 27' (labeled 'The Fourth Sunday of Easter', but the actual 4th Sunday of Easter is Apr 26, 2026). These read as the diocese's own date typos (a slipped +2 for the October pair, +1 for April), not a deliberate shift, but per this corpus's rule against silently correcting a source, all three are recorded with the literal date text printed in the source (2026-10-20, 2026-10-27, 2026-04-27) rather than the calendrically 'correct' Sunday.

Every other row's printed liturgical label was independently checked against its own printed date and found internally consistent (correct day-of-week and correct sequential count), including the two November All Saints'-week rows and the several places where the source's own wording departs from its usual pattern (e.g. 'July 26' spelled out in full rather than abbreviated 'Jul 26' as every neighboring month header is, and 'Apr 5 -Easter Day' using a bare unspaced hyphen where every other date header uses a spaced en dash '–') -- these wording/punctuation quirks are preserved verbatim in `liturgicalNote` but did not themselves indicate a wrong date.

Capitalization/wording inconsistencies in the source's own liturgical labels, preserved verbatim rather than normalized: 'The Twenty-third Sunday after Pentecost' (Nov 16, 2025, lowercase 'third', unlike every other Twenty-Nth label on the page which capitalizes the ordinal word); 'All Saints' Sunday (Twenty-First Sunday after Pentecost)' (Nov 2, 2025) lacking the leading 'The' that the otherwise-parallel 'All Saints' Sunday (The Twenty-Third Sunday after Pentecost)' (Nov 1, 2026) carries.

Typos/spelling inconsistencies among subject names, preserved verbatim rather than corrected: 'St. Albans School for Boys' (Aug 16) printed with no apostrophe, unlike every other 'St. Alban's'/'St. Albans'' possessive elsewhere on the page (e.g. 'St. Alban's Church, DC'); a stray extra space before the closing parenthesis in 'Labor Day (Sep 7 ):' (Sep 6) and 'International Earth Day (April 22 )' (Apr 19); the trailing stray comma before the parenthetical in 'Diocesan Convention: The Bishop, Convention Officers, Clerical and Lay Delegates, (January 26-27)' (Jan 25).

Bilingual/dual-name congregations sharing one building and one `place` are recorded as a SINGLE parish subject with both names joined exactly as the source joins them, per this corpus's existing precedent for the same situation (episcopal-southern-ohio-2026.json's 'Church of Our Saviour/La Iglesia de Nuestro Salvador', episcopal-rhode-island-2026.json's 'La Iglesia de la Ascension / The Church of the Ascension', episcopal-western-massachusetts-2026.json's 'St. Mark's/Iglesia Episcopal San Marcos') -- with the shared place text pulled out of the printed name and into the `place` field rather than left embedded and duplicated: 'St. Alban's Church, DC, and Iglesia San Alban' (Jun 14) -> name "St. Alban's Church and Iglesia San Alban", place "DC"; 'Church of the Ascension, Gaithersburg and Iglesia La Ascención' (May 10) -> name "Church of the Ascension and Iglesia La Ascención", place "Gaithersburg"; 'Church of Our Saviour, Hillandale and Nuestro Salvador' (Jul 26) -> name "Church of Our Saviour and Nuestro Salvador", place "Hillandale". 'St. Stephen and the Incarnation /San Esteban y La Encarnación, DC' (Dec 21, 2025) is transcribed as one parish (name "St. Stephen and the Incarnation /San Esteban y La Encarnación", place "DC") on the same reasoning, though here the leading 'and' is part of the congregation's own English dedication name (a real DC parish, 'St. Stephen and the Incarnation') rather than a list conjunction -- the bilingual half is only the '/San Esteban...' portion.

A different judgment call for a NAMED CHAPEL trailing after a parish with no place of its own: read as one associated chapel-of-ease under the same parish (a common structure for old Maryland/Southern-Maryland parishes) and folded into a single combined parish subject, with the shared place pulled into `place`: 'St. Thomas' Church, Upper Marlboro, and the Chapel of the Incarnation' (Dec 14, 2025) -> name "St. Thomas' Church and the Chapel of the Incarnation", place "Upper Marlboro"; 'Trinity Church, Newport & Hughesville, and Old Fields Chapel' (May 31) -> name "Trinity Church and Old Fields Chapel", place "Newport & Hughesville"; 'Trinity Church, St. Mary's City, and St. Mary's Chapel' (May 31) -> name "Trinity Church and St. Mary's Chapel", place "St. Mary's City". By contrast, 'St. Paul's Church, Baden, and St. Mary's Chapel, Aquasco' (Jan 25) prints TWO distinct places (Baden and Aquasco), so it was split into two separate parish subjects instead of combined, since each half is anchored to its own named place rather than sharing one.

Where the source's own comma-separated second half of a parish line is itself a historic civil-parish name rather than an ordinary town (e.g. 'Christ Church, Washington Parish'; 'St. John's Church, Zion Parish'; 'Grace Church, Silver Spring Parish'), that text is still recorded verbatim in the `place` field exactly as printed, on the same reasoning as every ordinary town name -- this corpus's `place` field is whatever the source prints after the comma, not necessarily a literal municipality. Conversely, several parish names print the word 'Parish' as part of the congregation's own name BEFORE the comma instead (e.g. 'St. Bartholomew's Parish, Laytonsville'; 'St. Margaret's Parish, DC'; 'St. Nicholas' Parish, Germantown'; 'Christ Church King & Queen Parish, Chaptico'; 'Christ Church Durham Parish, Nanjemoy'; 'Christ Church Port Tobacco Parish, La Plata') -- both patterns coexist in the same source and are each transcribed on their own printed side of the comma, without normalizing one convention into the other.

Type judgment call, matching this corpus's own episcopal-tennessee-2026.json precedent: entries naming a school, preschool, day school, or child-development center are recorded as `type: "category"` (full text as printed, including any trailing place, kept together in `name` since `category` carries no separate `place` field) rather than `type: "parish"`, even when several are formatted identically to an ordinary Name-comma-Place parish line -- e.g. 'St. Columba's Nursery School, DC'; 'St. James' Children's School, Potomac'; 'St. Matthew's Day School, Hyattsville'; 'St. John's Church Georgetown Preschool'; 'St. John's Episcopal School, Olney'; 'Good Shepherd Episcopal Preschool, Silver Spring'; 'St. Patrick's Episcopal Day School, DC'; 'St. Philip's Child Development Center, DC'; and the five schools grouped on Aug 16 (St. Albans School for Boys; The National Cathedral School for Girls; Beauvoir, the National Cathedral Elementary School; Washington Episcopal School; The Bishop John T. Walker School). 'St. Andrew's Episcopal School and St. Andrew's Lower School, Potomac' (Nov 30, 2025) was kept as a single combined category (both schools sharing one trailing place, on the same reasoning as the associated-chapel calls above) rather than split into two.

Congregation-sounding names printed with NO place/town at all were recorded as `type: "category"` rather than `parish`, since this schema requires a non-empty `place` for `parish` and this corpus does not fabricate one: 'St. Barnabas' Church of the Deaf' (Jun 7); 'The Cathedral Church of St. Peter and St. Paul' and 'Cathedral Chaplains and Cathedral Volunteers' (Jun 28, evidently Washington National Cathedral, but no place is printed against it); 'St. Luke's House, Bethesda' (Oct 20) was kept as `category` despite carrying a place, since 'House' reads as a service ministry rather than a worshiping congregation, distinguishing it from the parish 'St. Luke's Church, Bethesda' and 'St. Luke's Parish, DC' printed in the same entry.

'Pray for children's health and for healthcare workers for all children' and the following line '(Oct 5 – Child Health Day)' (Oct 4) are printed as two separate line breaks in the source's own markup but were merged into one category subject here, read as a single prayer intention whose date annotation simply wrapped to its own line -- the same pattern the source elsewhere keeps on one line (e.g. 'Independence Day (July 4) Pray for dignity, justice, and freedom for all.', Jun 28).

'African Palms' (Mar 29) and 'St. Mary's Court' (May 24) are transcribed verbatim as categories with no further identification available from the source; their exact referents (a fair-trade palm-sourcing program and, presumably, a senior-living facility grouped with the other named senior ministries in that same entry) were not independently verified beyond what the source itself names.

The source's own two monthly Spanish-language and Armed Forces/Federal cycle-of-prayer links, and its link to the separate worldwide Anglican Cycle of Prayer, are not part of the Diocese of Washington's own local cycle transcribed here and are excluded, the same reasoning as this corpus's existing episcopal-tennessee-2026.json exclusion of the same worldwide-cycle link (already covered separately by this corpus's own scope-'communion' file).
